newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power flat to higher ahead of cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power flat to higher ahead of cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. held steady or rose Thursday ahead of an Arctic blast seen arriving into the region this weekend.

Generating capacity remained tight with a number of power units in the region off line for seasonal maintenance. About 3,000 megawatts (MW) of capacity would remain out of service until the end of the month.
The Nine Mile Point nuclear unit 1 in Scriba, N.Y., which tripped off line late Tuesday due to a generator problem, was expected to resume operation this weekend.
Generation costs were stable as prices of residual fuel oil, used during peak demand production, held steady amid firm crude oil values.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Friday delivery remained in the $22.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Friday was still pegged at $13.50-$14.50.

The outage of Nine Mile Point 1 did not affect western NYPP prices because Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, which operates the nuclear unit, increased internal generation rather than buying power in the spot market to make up for the loss of the unit, market sources said.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Friday was notationally valued higher at $30.00-$31.00, better bid than Wednesday's $29.00-$31.00.
Off-peak, non-firm Friday electricity in eastern NYPP was again valued in the $16.00-$18.00 area.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted at $34.00-$35.00, higher than Friday's consensus range in the $31.00-$33.00 range.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was assessed at $21.00-$22.00, up from $18.00-$19.50 on Wednesday.

The New York Power Authority was scheduled to restore a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission power line from Quebec to New York after shutting two segments of the line last weekend for seasonal maintenance.
